title: Sichuan Home-Style Tofu with Peppers and Bamboo Shoots
summary: Crisp fried tofu is tossed through a glossy, chilli-spiked Sichuan-style sauce with peppers, carrot and bamboo shoots for a punchy, savoury stir-fry.

ingredients.item: green pepper, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
carrot, peeled and sliced 5 mm thick on the diagonal
canned sliced bamboo shoots, drained, rinsed and patted dry
spring onions, whites and greens sliced separately
piece fresh ginger (2.5 cm), peeled and cut into fine matchsticks

steps.title: Press
steps.text: Halve 400 g firm tofu lengthways, slice into 2 cm slabs, spread on kitchen paper and leave to dry for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Stir 2 tsp soy sauce, 2 tsp cornflour, 1 tsp sugar and 1 tsp vegetarian oyster sauce together in a small bowl.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat the frying oil in a wok to 190°C and fry the tofu in one layer, turning once, until crisp and deep golden, about 10 minutes, then drain on paper, lowering the tofu in carefully away from you.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pour off all but 3 tbsp of the oil, heat until just smoking, then cook the green pepper, carrot and bamboo shoots until crisp-tender, about 3 minutes.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Push the vegetables aside and fry the garlic, spring onion whites, ginger and doubanjiang in the gap for 30 seconds, mashing the paste in, then mix through.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add 180 ml water and the tofu, then toss gently for 3-5 minutes so the tofu soaks up some of the liquid.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Stir the sauce back in and toss for 30 seconds until glossy and thickened.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Scatter with the sliced spring onion greens and serve with rice.

tips: Pat the tofu really dry before frying so it crisps rather than spits in the hot oil.
Keep the oil at a steady medium-high heat so the tofu colours evenly without burning.
Have all the vegetables and aromatics prepped before you start, as the stir-fry moves quickly once the tofu is frying.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten fresh, but leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat in a hot pan or wok. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
